newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Turkey plan joint naval exercise.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Turkey plan joint naval exercise.

text.p: Turkish military officers met Israeli security officials on Monday to discuss joint naval exercises with the U.S. military, the Israeli defence ministry said.

A ministry statement said Turkish Deputy Chief of Staff General Cevik Bir, visiting Israel with a delegation of 23 senior officers, discussed the exercises and other issues of security cooperation with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
The statement quoted Mordechai as telling Bir he hoped the cooperation would "contribute to stability in the Middle East" and that he intended to deepen the links between the countries.

Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan was in Israel last week for security coordination. Turkey and Israel have signed defence cooperation pacts which drew an angry response from Iran and many in the Arab world.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan won Turkish elections partly on a promise to cut military ties to the Jewish state.

The Israeli statement quoted Bir as saying he "supported the need to strengthen and deepen security cooperation" and telling Mordechai he was impressed on visits to Israel Air Industries, a Merkava tank factory and other industrial projects.

"We heard and learned about and saw high-tech, state of the art technological ventures, pertaining to almost all areas of the military, and all of them developed and produced by Israel," the statement quoted Bir as saying.
